title: Commitment stress test and geocluster readout

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-11-02 14:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyer (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM), Marta Lopez (Tidefall Head of MLOps), Ethan Chu (VP Eng), Samir Khan (SRE), Nina Park (Procurement)

Summary (auto): Quick readout on Q1 spike patterns, ask for APAC geocluster, security docs request, agreed on 48hr stress test and pricing amendment.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we got Marta, Ethan, Samir, Nina, and on our side Priya and Liam. Is that right?
[00:12] Marta (Tidefall): Yep, that's right. Thanks Jordan. 
[00:18] Ethan (Tidefall): Sorry, ran a little late. Looks like an intense agenda though.
[00:22] Jordan: No worries. We wanted to do a renewal + expansion check — get ahead of the Q1 traffic surge you mentioned in the email and talk APAC geo-cluster options.
[00:34] Priya (Redwood): I'll jump into the technical bits — what patterns you expect, latency targets, and we'll map that to dedicated vs hosted burst options.
[00:42] Marta: Great. Big picture — our throughput for Q4 is steady, but marketing flagged a campaign early January that's likely to double token volume for a 10‑day window, with 3 hour peaks in the morning traffic. We also want lower latencies for APAC customers, currently routed to US-west and that's killing perc95 for some routes.
[00:58] Samir: To add, our SREs want an automated failover across geo clusters — if APAC capacity is saturated we need predictable fallback to EU or US with a soft degrade, not a hard 500.
[01:12] Priya: Makes sense. Two quick clarifications — typical sequence lengths and KV cache hit rates? Those change batching behavior.
[01:20] Marta: Average sequences are 120 tokens, worst-case 400, and KV hit is around 60% because we use some prefix caching in prod.
[01:28] Priya: OK 120 median, 400 tail, 60% KV — that helps. For the double volume spike, we usually recommend reserved dedicated capacity for the baseline and then hosted burst or autoscale for the short window. Dedicated gives predictable latency but costs a bit more.
[01:42] Ethan: We were hoping to avoid long-term reserved spend — can Redwood guarantee fallbacks? What's the SLA behavior when burst exceeds reserved capacity?
[01:50] Jordan: We have automated fallback policies — priority routing, model variant fallbacks (small quantized variant) and region fallback. If reserved is exhausted, we can route to hosted pool but you'll see higher cost and slightly higher latency. For hard SLO guarantees you'd want a dedicated buffer.
[02:06] Nina (Procurement): From procurement side we need to understand contract amendment language for burst capacity and regional additions — e.g., how to cap spend and notifications.
[02:14] Liam (CSM): We'll propose a 20% safety headroom on top of your forecast and a notification cadence: threshold alerts at 60/80/95% of committed. Also per-token spend caps can be included.
[02:26] Marta: That 20% sounds reasonable. Can you walk through the APAC geo-cluster options — private VPC vs managed? We have data residency concerns in APAC‑NZ and need KMS control.
[02:38] Priya: Sure. Two paths: Redwood Private (VPC/on‑prem) where you retain the control plane in your network and integrate with your KMS/HSM, or Hosted with VPC peering and customer-managed keys via KMS federation. The Private option gives stronger isolation but a longer lead time for provisioning.
[02:58] Samir: Lead time estimate? Our calendar is tight — need APAC readiness by Jan 3rd for the campaign.
[03:04] Priya: For Private—depending on region and whether we ship on-prem, it can be 6-8 weeks typically. For hosted with VPC peering + KMS, we can often do 2-3 weeks for onboarding, assuming peering approvals and certs.
[03:18] Ethan: Hmm, 6-8 weeks is risky. So hosted with peering might be the only feasible option for Jan 3rd. What about perf — will APAC latency improve enough over US-west?
[03:26] Priya: Yes — with an APAC edge region (hosted) you'll likely see p95 drop from ~420ms to ~95-140ms depending on model. We'll need to validate with a bench run using your traffic pattern.
[03:38] Marta: Can Redwood do that bench run from our APAC test agents and give us the results?
[03:42] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll run an APAC latency bench and a 48-hour stress test using your sample traffic to validate p95 and costs. Priya will own the stress test.
[03:52] Samir: On security, we need SOC2 Type II evidence, SSO/SAML setup docs, and examples of audit logs with retention controls. Also KMS integration — we need to ensure Redwood never has plaintext access to keys.
[04:06] Liam: We'll package the SOC2 report, a SAML SSO guide and an HSM/KMS integration note. For hosted with KMS federation, keys live in customer KMS; Redwood only gets wrapped tokens. We'll also include sample audit log entries for token-level access.
[04:20] Nina: Good. Procurement will need the full security packet to greenlight the amendment. Can you share by Thursday?
[04:26] Liam: Yes, we'll get that by Thursday.
[04:30] Ethan: Back to pricing — how does the 20% headroom get reflected? Do we pay for reserved plus a burst pool hourly, or do you invoice post-fact with overage?
[04:40] Jordan: Options — A) reserved monthly commit with burst hourly billed at a higher rate, B) tiered committed plus pre-bought burst credits, or C) short-term reserved uplift for January. We'll draft an amendment showing the three options and cost implications.
[04:56] Marta: I like option C for simplicity if the uplift cost is reasonable for a month. Otherwise B could work. We can't do per-minute surprises.
[05:04] Priya: Technically, if you choose uplift we can pin model versions and kernel configs to maximize throughput; otherwise burst routes might pick quantized variants which can change output characteristics slightly — that matters if you have deterministic prompts.
[05:18] Samir: That point's important. We have some critical prompts where output regression could break downstream parsing. Can Redwood run a regressions check as part of the stress test?
[05:26] Priya: Yes — we can include a quality regression set. If we see drift beyond the agreed tolerance we'll flag and optionally pin a non-quantized variant for those routes.
[05:34] Ethan: Workflow wise — we need results by Nov 10 to make a decision and have procurement sign by Nov 20. Is that feasible?
[05:40] Jordan: Totally feasible. We're aligning internal ops to hit that.
[05:44] Marta: A couple of nitty-gritty items — egress/cost visibility, token-level cost breakdown, and tracing hooks during the stress run.
[05:54] Liam: We'll enable token-level billing for the test and provide a Prometheus trace hook you can scrape. For egress, we'll show estimated bandwidth numbers for APAC region during the 10‑day window.
[06:06] Nina: On legal, any changes to the indemnity or data residency language for the regional addendum? Our counsel will need to review.
[06:12] Jordan: The standard regional addendum adds a data residency clause and KMS controls; indemnities remain the same but we'll flag anything unusual to your counsel. We'll share a redlined amendment.
[06:22] Marta: Good. One more question — if APAC is saturated and you route to EU fallback, is there an option to degrade only non-critical routes? We have routes labeled critical and non-critical.
[06:34] Priya: Yes we can map routing policies per route/model. You can set a priority tag; non-critical routes get lower precedence for reserved capacity and be routed to cheaper/quantized variants first.
[06:44] Samir: Perfect, that'll keep the checkout flow snappy.
[06:48] Ethan: Any blockers we should be aware of?
[06:50] Priya: Only the peering approvals and sample trace. Also model pinning for critical routes requires an extra step in deployment config — we'll walk you through it.
[06:58] Marta: I'll get the sample trace to Priya by COB Friday.
[07:02] Jordan: Great — recap: Priya runs 48-hour stress test with quality regression; Liam sends security packet; Jordan drafts pricing amendment with options; Marta provides sample traffic. We'll target results by Nov 10.
[07:16] Nina: From procurement I'll review the amendment draft and we may ask for an initial PO for the uplift.
[07:20] Jordan: Totally fine. Anything else?
[07:22] Ethan: Quick note on competitor conversation — we're also evaluating an in-house serving option for the burst window with spot instances. Cost looks similar but operational risk is higher. We wanted to surface that for Redwood.
[07:36] Jordan: Understood. We'll include a short cost vs operations comparison in the amendment.
[07:42] Priya: I'll also include expected latency numbers for the quantized variant vs full-precision so you can see potential regressions.
[07:50] Marta: Thanks. One last ask — can Redwood provide an emergency runbook if we see an unexpected 5x spike in traffic?
[07:58] Liam: Yes, we have a runbook with auto-scaling and manual escalation paths — we'll attach it.
[08:04] Jordan: Ok wrapping up. We'll follow up with links: pricing draft (internal link), security packet (secure link), and a scheduling poll for the APAC bench run.
[08:14] Liam: Links: Pricing draft (https://redwood.example/tdl/amendment-draft), Security packet (https://redwood.example/tdl/security-packet), Bench scheduling poll (https://cal.com/redwood/apac-bench).
[08:24] Marta: Got it — we'll coordinate. Thanks everyone.
[08:28] Jordan: Thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript.

Notes / misc: occasional transcription artifacts — 'KV cash' appears in automated notes, SAMEL typo for SAML in earlier auto-summaries; confirm correct acronyms in the packet.
